RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the May 7, 2002/Vaisakha 17, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Commerce and Industry; Finance; Petroleum and
Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture; Water Resources)
Total number of questions—20
Cut in CNG supply to industrial units
*581. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Compressed
Natural Gas supply to many industrial
houses has been cut to meet its increased
demand in Delhi;
(b) if so, the loss of production of
industrial units with depleted CNG supply;
(c) by when the Indraprastha Gas Ltd.
(I.G.L.) will be able to meet the full
requirement of Delhi; and
(d) the steps taken to increase the supply
of Compressed Natural Gas to industrial
units?
Income tax dues from sports
personalities
*582. SHRI H.K. JAVARE GOWDA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of income tax dues from
sports personalities in the country for the
last three years;
(b) the number of cricketers who were
assessed for income tax and the amount due
from them for the last three years; and
(c) the details of tax paid under open
inquiry made by the income tax department
as reported in Deccan Herald dated
18th April, 2002?
Water share of Gujarat in Indus river
†*583. SHRIMATI SAVITA
SHARDA: Will the Minister of  WATER
RESOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Government of Gujarat has demanded its
share in water of river the Indus;
(b) if so, whether Government have so
far given consideration to the demand; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, by
when the same is likely to be considered?
Performance of oil companies in post
APM regime
*584. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of public sector oil
companies which would suffer loss in the

177
WIN2\SESSION\518RS-QUES 177
month of April with the dismantling of APM
from the first of April and his instructions
to the oil companies to maintain the prices
of petroleum products constantly;
(b) the amount of profit the stand-alone
refineries in the private sector would make
after dismantling of APM in the month of
April; and
(c) in what manner Government propose
to balance the increase in cost of crude oil
and selling of petro products in the open
market at international parity?
LPG agency at Tirupattur in Tamil
Nadu
*585. SHRIMATI S. G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
problems faced by LPG consumers in
Tirupattur and surrounding areas in
Sivaganga district of  Tamil Nadu due to
non-availability of LPG agencies in that
area;
(b) if so, whether LPG agencies are
proposed to be set up at Tirupattur;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Excise duty on bicycle parts
*586. SHRI SUKHDEV SINGH
LIBRA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
representation from United Cycle and Parts
Manufacturers’ Association, Ludhiana
(Punjab) requesting the Central Government
to reconsider the imposition of excise duty
on bicycle and its parts;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what is Government's reaction
thereto?
I.T. return of M/s Buildmore India
Ltd. and Skipper Corner
*587. SHRI DARA SINGH
CHAUHAN: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether M/s Buildmore India
Limited, B1-A, Ajit Singh House, Plot No.
12, DDA Commercial Complex, Yusuf
Sarai and Skipper Corner, 88 Nehru Place,
New Delhi, are regularly filing IT returns
and paying taxes;
(b) if so, the details thereof for the last
three years;
(c) whether there are large scale
discrepancies in their returns as they are
fleecing public by getting money from them
and promising residential flats but not a
single construction has been made by them
nor they are returning money to public; if
so, the details thereof; and
(d) if the answer to part (a) above be in
the negative, the action taken/proposed
against them?
Development of tourist circuits
*588. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO: Will the Minister of  TOURISM
AND CULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to develop three tourist circuits through
foreign agencies;
(b) if so, what are the names of three
circuits and by when the work on their
development is likely to commence; and
(c) the work which will be entrusted to
foreign agencies?

IB report on airport security
4228.  SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item which appeared
in the Statesman dated 2nd February, 2002
captioned "IB report slams lax airport
security";
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto;
(c) the major highlights of the IB report;
and
(d) the steps proposed to be taken to
tone up the security arrangements in the
concerned airports including the Indira
Gandhi International Airport?
Request for purchase of aircrafts
4229. SHRI  BHAGATRAM
MANHAR:
SHRI DEVI PRASAD SINGH:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a)  what are the names of the Airlines
which have requested the Government for
purchase of aircrafts;
(b) what are the details of the proposal
submitted by these Airlines; and
(c) whether Government have asked
these Airlines to submit the source of funding
of these aircrafts and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Air services on Delhi-Raipur-
Jabalpur-Delhi Sector
†4230. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the average number of persons
travelling per day during the last one year
by Delhi-Raipur-Jabalpur-Delhi flight of the
Alliance Air;
(b) the reasons for reducing one day in
its total number of flight days;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
further increase the number of flight days
and whether there is also any scheme for
expansion of Delhi-Raipur-Jabalpur-Delhi
flight; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?

Enquiries conducted by COSCA
4231. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
Commissioner of Security Civil Aviation
(COSCA) in the Bureau of Civil Aviation
Security (BCAS) has been authorised to
conduct enquiries of other Government
institutions and officers in addition to his
present duties;
(b) if so, the details of enquiries being
conducted by COSCA of officers other than
working in BCAS;
(c) whether prior permission of the
Ministry was obtained before accepting to
act as Inquiry Officer of other Ministries/
Institutions; and
(d) if not, the action taken or proposed
to be taken against COSCA?
Ground handling services at Delhi
Airport
4232. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of agencies which are
authorised to handle the ground activities at
Delhi Airport;
(b) whether the Bureau of Civil Aviation
Security (BCAS) has carried out any survey
in the recent past to find out the unauthorised
agencies;
(c) if so, what is the outcome of the
survey; and
(d) what is the strategy to check the entry
of these unauthorised agencies?
Operational airports in A.P.
4233. DR. DASARI NARAYANA
RAO: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the airports/airstrips in Andhra
Pradesh which are maintained by Airports
Authority of India but are not operational at
present;
(b) what are the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps Government have taken to
make them operational?
Sales tax on Aviation Turbine Fuel
†4234. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the sales tax levied on
Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF), State-wise;
(b) whether Government have requested
the States to reduce the sales tax on ATF;
(c) if so, the number of States which
have taken steps to reduce the sales tax; and
(d) the steps taken byGovernment to levy
sales tax at uniform rate on ATF in all States
and to reduce its rate?
Fly-by-night aviation clubs
4235. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned "Want
a licence to fly? Shell out Rs. 19 lakh in
Mumbai" which appeared in The Indian
Express dated the 16th April, 2002;
(b) if so, what is Government's reaction
thereto;
(c) whether these fly-by-night aviation

Central Government;
(d) whether these clubs have
infrastructure for flying;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, whether Government would
ban such clubs which jeopardise the lives
of trainees?
